words.sense: take another person’s office or authority without legal right
misconceptions: Treating any removal from office as a seizure of that office.

words.sense: remove a person from office without necessarily taking it
misconceptions: Thinking a wrongful seizure is merely getting someone removed.

semantic_axes.description: Usurp means take another person’s authority without the right to it; oust means force that person out without necessarily taking the role.

edges.boundary_rule: Usurp means take another person’s authority without the right to it; oust means force that person out without necessarily taking the role.
clues_a: uses a false claim of authority
clues_b: removes a leader without replacement by actor

misconceptions.M1: Confuses usurp with oust by overlooking the defining difference: Usurp means take another person’s authority without the right to it; oust means force that person out without necessarily taking the role.
misconceptions.M2: Assumes evidence for oust necessarily proves usurp; these are different tests.
misconceptions.M3: Overweights a later superficial detail instead of retaining or appropriately updating the original boundary evidence.

chains.frame: Which word best describes Jaya’s action involving the club chair?

beats.text: Jaya changed the club roster to name herself chair, though nobody had elected her.
beats.decisive_clue: claimed another person’s chairmanship without election
beats.reason: Taking the chair herself without authority is the deciding feature.

beats.text: She also hid the minutes recording the actual election.
beats.decisive_clue: concealed the elected chair’s right to the post
beats.reason: Hiding the minutes reinforces the wrongful takeover rather than simply removing someone.

chains.feedback_short: Concealed the elected chair’s right to the post; hiding the minutes reinforces the wrongful takeover rather than simply removing someone.
chains.feedback_deep: Usurp means take another person’s office or authority without legal right; oust means remove a person from office without necessarily taking it. Hiding the minutes reinforces the wrongful takeover rather than simply removing someone.
chains.contrast_rule: Usurp means take another person’s authority without the right to it; oust means force that person out without necessarily taking the role.

chains.frame: Which word best describes Omar’s action against the chess captain?

beats.text: Omar organized a successful vote to remove the captain after repeated missed practices.
beats.decisive_clue: arranged the captain’s removal through a vote
beats.reason: The action dislodged the incumbent but did not seize their authority.

beats.text: He then supported an election in which he was not a candidate.
beats.decisive_clue: did not take the vacated position himself
beats.reason: A separate election confirms Omar did not take the post.

chains.feedback_short: Did not take the vacated position himself; a separate election confirms Omar did not take the post.
chains.feedback_deep: Usurp means take another person’s office or authority without legal right; oust means remove a person from office without necessarily taking it. A separate election confirms Omar did not take the post.
chains.contrast_rule: Usurp means take another person’s authority without the right to it; oust means force that person out without necessarily taking the role.

chains.frame: Which word best describes Camila’s claim to the committee presidency?

beats.text: Camila used a former officer’s login to announce that she, not the elected president, now ran the committee.
beats.decisive_clue: assumed an elected officer’s power without a right
beats.reason: The claim takes authority belonging to another person.

beats.text: She repeated the announcement on a second school noticeboard.
beats.decisive_clue: assumed an elected officer’s power without a right
beats.reason: Repetition does not change the unauthorized nature of the same claim.

chains.feedback_short: Assumed an elected officer’s power without a right; repetition does not change the unauthorized nature of the same claim.
chains.feedback_deep: Usurp means take another person’s office or authority without legal right; oust means remove a person from office without necessarily taking it. Repetition does not change the unauthorized nature of the same claim.
chains.contrast_rule: Usurp means take another person’s authority without the right to it; oust means force that person out without necessarily taking the role.

chains.frame: Which word best describes Noura’s action toward the house treasurer?

beats.text: Noura convinced her flatmates to vote the treasurer out for missing payments.
Her written proposal called for a fresh vote to choose someone else.
beats.decisive_clue: called for a separate successor rather than taking the office
beats.reason: Her proposal shows the vacancy was not a claim to the treasurer’s authority.

chains.frame: Which word best describes Kenji’s action regarding the fundraiser leader?

beats.text: Kenji printed badges naming himself fundraiser leader while another volunteer still held the elected role.
beats.decisive_clue: asserted a role that rightfully belonged to another volunteer
beats.reason: He claimed another person’s authority without a legitimate transfer.

beats.decisive_clue: asserted a role that rightfully belonged to another volunteer
beats.reason: The timing confirms no appointment authorized his claim.
